question: What is the maximum deduction an individual can claim for life insurance premium and provident fund contributions under the new Income-tax Act?
ground_truth: An individual or Hindu undivided family can deduct the aggregate of eligible payments listed in Schedule XV, up to a maximum of Rs. 150,000 in the tax year, under Section 123.

question: Can the total of all deductions under Chapter VIII exceed a taxpayer's gross total income?
ground_truth: No. Section 122(2) states the aggregate amount of deductions under Chapter VIII shall not, in any case, exceed the gross total income of the assessee.

question: How much can an employee deduct for employer contributions to a Central Government pension scheme?
ground_truth: Under Section 124(1), the deduction is the whole amount contributed by the employer up to 14% of salary if the employer is the Central or State Government, or 10% of salary for any other employer.

question: What deduction is available for medical treatment expenses of a dependant with a disability?
ground_truth: Section 127(1) allows a resident individual or HUF a deduction of up to Rs. 75,000 from gross total income for expenditure on medical treatment, training and rehabilitation of a dependant with a disability, or amounts paid into an approved LIC/insurer maintenance scheme for that dependant.

question: What deduction can a person with a severe disability claim for themselves?
ground_truth: Section 154(1) allows a resident individual certified as a person with severe disability to deduct Rs. 125,000 while computing total income (Rs. 75,000 for disability that is not severe).

question: Is a deduction under Section 154 available without a medical certificate?
ground_truth: No. Section 154(2) requires the individual to furnish a copy of the certificate issued by a medical authority, and to furnish a fresh certificate if the original expires and needs reassessment, along with the return of income under Section 263.

question: Can a company claim a deduction meant for individuals under Section 123?
ground_truth: No. Section 123 restricts this deduction to an individual or a Hindu undivided family; the retrieved context does not extend this deduction to companies.

question: What happens if profits from an eligible start-up business are already claimed as a deduction under Part C of Chapter VIII?
ground_truth: Under Section 122(4), where profits from an eligible business are claimed and allowed as a deduction under Part C for a tax year, no deduction for the same profits is allowed under any other provision of the Act for that year, and the deduction cannot exceed the profits of that undertaking or business.

question: Can I claim a deduction for my child's tuition fees?
ground_truth: Yes. Tuition fees (excluding development fees, donations or similar payments) paid by an individual to a university, college, school or other educational institution in India for the full-time education of up to two children qualify under Schedule XV for the deduction under Section 123, within its overall limit.

question: What is the deduction for interest on an education loan?
ground_truth: Section 129 allows an individual a deduction for interest paid in the tax year on a loan from a financial institution or approved charitable institution taken for higher education of the individual or a relative, for the initial tax year and up to seven immediately succeeding tax years, or until the interest is fully paid, whichever is earlier.

When am I considered resident in India?
ground_truth: Under Section 6(2), an individual is resident in India in a tax year if they are in India for 182 days or more in that year, or for 60 days or more in that year and 365 days or more in the four preceding years.

question: What is the standard deduction for salaried employees?
ground_truth: Section 19(1) allows a standard deduction of ₹75,000 or the salary, whichever is less, where tax is computed under the new regime in Section 202(1), and ₹50,000 or the salary, whichever is less, in any other case.

question: What are the income-tax slab rates under the new tax regime?
Is income up to 12 lakh tax-free under the new regime?
ground_truth: For a resident individual taxed under Section 202(1), Section 156(2) gives a rebate of 100% of the tax or ₹60,000, whichever is less, where total income does not exceed ₹12 lakh, so no tax is payable; just above ₹12 lakh, marginal relief limits the tax to the amount by which income exceeds ₹12 lakh.

question: How does presumptive taxation work for a small business?
ground_truth: Under Section 58(2), an eligible assessee (resident individual, HUF or non-LLP firm) with turnover up to ₹2 crore (₹3 crore if cash receipts are at most 5%) can declare profit of 6% of turnover received through banking or online modes and 8% of the rest, or actual profit if higher.

question: What deductions are allowed from rental income from a house?
ground_truth: Section 22(1) allows 30% of the annual value, and interest payable on capital borrowed to acquire, construct, repair, renew or reconstruct the property.

question: What is the tax rate on long-term capital gains?
ground_truth: Section 197(1) taxes long-term capital gains at 12.5%, with the rest of the total income taxed as if it were the whole total income.
